nodes.label: Firewall
nodes.description: Network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing traffic using configurable security rules.

nodes.label: Network Traffic

nodes.label: Trusted Network

nodes.label: VLAN
nodes.description: Network segment that can be separated by a firewall.

nodes.label: Host-based Firewall

nodes.label: LAN

nodes.label: WAN

nodes.label: Virtual Appliance

nodes.label: Virtual Host

nodes.label: VPN

nodes.label: Packet Filter

nodes.label: UDP

nodes.label: Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC)

nodes.label: 1987 Firewall Technology Paper

nodes.label: Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory
nodes.description: Institution associated with the BPF paper.

nodes.label: Transport Layer
nodes.description: OSI layer 4 context for tracked conversations.

nodes.label: Protocol Abuse

nodes.label: Next-generation Firewall

nodes.label: Process

nodes.label: Process ID

nodes.label: Network Service

nodes.label: Service Access Control

nodes.label: Application Awareness

nodes.label: Compliance Requirements

nodes.label: Directory Service

nodes.label: LDAP

nodes.label: RADIUS

nodes.label: TACACS+

nodes.label: User-to-IP Mapping

nodes.label: Firewall Configuration

nodes.label: Configuration Error

source_claims.claim: Firewall monitors and controls network traffic using configurable rules.
Firewall separates trusted/untrusted networks or VLANs.
Packet filters use ACLs and packet attributes/actions.
1987 firewall paper described DEC packet-filter systems.
Application firewalls understand application protocols and detect non-standard ports/protocol abuse.
NGFW expands inspection and adds listed security features.
Endpoint application firewalls filter by process ID/socket calls.
Rules evaluate direction, source, destination, port, protocol, applications, and action.
Zones group devices by security requirements and govern traffic.
User ID enables identity-based rules and directory integration.
School example denies Students access to social media while default LAN→WAN traffic is allowed.
Configuration is complex/error-prone and misconfiguration can create security issues.
Policy reduces exposure to unauthorized access, malware, and cyberattack.
PIX combined firewall/NAT and was later succeeded by ASA.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Stateful filtering adds conversation knowledge to packet filtering.
Stateful filtering tracks conversations; application filtering understands protocols.
NGFW broadens application/deep inspection with additional features.
Network firewall sits between networks; host firewall runs on a host.
Virtual appliance runs on a virtual host controlled by a hypervisor.
Policy is a collection of rules; a rule is an individual decision specification.
Zone is a logical security grouping, not necessarily a physical network.
Service is port/protocol-oriented; application is software/L7-oriented.
IP identifies network addressing; User ID identifies an individual identity.
Both are listed as refusal/discard actions but remain separate labels in the source.
PIX combines both, but they are separate mechanisms.
Relative trust distinction across a firewall boundary.
Configuration defines controls; enforcement applies them.

misconceptions.misconception: A firewall is only a packet filter.
misconceptions.correction: The source includes stateful, application, endpoint, and next-generation firewall mechanisms.

misconceptions.misconception: A firewall must use dedicated hardware.
misconceptions.correction: The source includes software appliances on general-purpose hardware and virtual appliances.

misconceptions.misconception: Network-based and host-based firewalls have the same placement.
misconceptions.correction: Network-based firewalls sit between networks; host-based firewalls run directly on hosts.

misconceptions.misconception: Application firewalls only inspect port numbers.
misconceptions.correction: They can understand application protocols and detect non-standard ports/protocol abuse.

misconceptions.misconception: User ID is simply an IP address.
misconceptions.correction: User ID adds identity-based policy and is mapped to network activity.

misconceptions.misconception: A firewall zone is necessarily a physical network.
misconceptions.correction: The source defines zones as logical segments grouped by security requirements.

misconceptions.misconception: LAN-to-WAN and WAN-to-LAN have the same default.
misconceptions.correction: The source gives allow LAN→WAN and drop WAN→LAN as typical defaults.
The source describes configuration as complex and error-prone.

misconceptions.misconception: NGFW and NAT are the same thing.
misconceptions.correction: PIX combined firewall and NAT; NGFW is an inspection/security evolution.

misconceptions.misconception: Firewall rules use only IP addresses.
misconceptions.correction: Rules may use direction, source, destination, port, protocol, applications, and action.
